stage: beat reachability, and the assumption behind it, verified from the engine

result.the_assumption_now_verified: an earlier stage of mine dismissed thirteen findings by treating a beat id as a runtime state key rather than an authored record. That was an assumption; it is now read from the engine - beat.set-state writes into the beats map by beatId (ContentRuleEngine lines 75-76) and beat.state reads it back (line 262) - so the dismissal was right and is no longer a guess
result.the_mirror_check: the same reasoning that found seventeen unreachable fact gates applies here: a condition on a beat nobody writes can never become true. Measured: twenty-six beats written, seven read, and ZERO unreachable reads, so every beat condition has a writer today
result.the_reverse_case_reported_not_judged: six or more beats are written and never read. That is NOT reported as a defect: a beat may exist for the journal or for an act that is not authored yet, and the notes say so
result.why_the_direction_matters: the two cases look alike and are opposites: no writer means a dead condition, no reader means a state nobody asks about. Only the first is a defect, and the notes say which is which
